source.title: AnalogVNN: A fully modular framework for modeling and optimizing photonic neural networks

record.tranche_reason: The study trains simulated analog image classifiers and reports classification accuracy and learning outcomes, but does not measure training classification error, which is the outcome named by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy, not training error. Its explicit statements about whether learning occurs and its reported test accuracies bear on training outcomes, but do not establish whether training error reaches zero or near zero. The paper does not report results for the specific initialization, shortcut, learning-rate stability, or batch-normalization comparisons in the versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures test accuracy of simulated analog classifiers under precision, noise, activation and normalization choices. These results do not measure any claim version's specified effect. Citing batch-normalization research and mentioning exploratory batch-normalization tests do not establish training-speed or learning-rate-tolerance results.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that AnalogVNN helps optimize simulated photonic networks, that weight precision and noise are more consequential than input precision and noise, and that GeLU and SiLU perform best at higher noise. They do not establish near-zero training error or any other claim version.
record.recipe_differences: Simulates analog noise, limited precision, and normalization while training image classifiers; it does not reproduce the claim's stated digital-network training-error experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset complexity, model depth, activation, normalization, precision, noise, and batch size affect reported test accuracy; the paper states batch size strongly affects the 9-layer model.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight precision and noise affect analog classifiers' test accuracy more strongly than input precision and noise. The authors report that their 9-layer CIFAR-10 model requires at least 4-bit weight precision for learning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight precision and noise constrain learning and test accuracy in the tested simulated analog classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report 58.67% maximum CIFAR-10 test accuracy after 10 epochs and 77% after 50 epochs, without specifying a matched configuration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Longer training can improve test accuracy in the tested small analog CIFAR-10 classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: Clamp and L2 weight normalization and activation choices affect 9-layer model test accuracy; these are not initialization comparisons or measurements of batch-normalization acceleration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation and signal-normalization choices affect accuracy in simulated analog networks, particularly under noise and reduced precision.

record.problems: The reported outcomes relevant here are test accuracies rather than training errors. Several accuracy results are presented only in figures, and no training-error values are supplied.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows. Figure-only accuracies without an explicit prose value are represented only where the paper states the result is relevant; the remaining plotted conditions were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, corrupted or random labels, and training-error dependence on size, early stopping or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth, identity-shortcut comparisons and the specified initialization alternatives.
Initialization comparisons measuring learning speed, signal or gradient propagation, or trainable depth.
Loss recovery above initial stability limits, curvature changes, divergence and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The isolated Figure 7a caption mentions training accuracy, but its color-versus-grayscale comparison does not test any version. No verdict follows from poor test accuracy alone.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report training classification error, random-label results, or a comparison of model size, early stopping, or regularized recipes by training error.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment, spurious-minimum measurement, or width comparison.
No plain-versus-residual shortcut comparison of training error across depth.
No comparison of initialization methods or trainable depth by initialization.
No learning-rate stability, loss-curvature, or sharpness experiment.
No batch-normalization versus no-normalization comparison of training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: 1- to 6-layer photonic analog image classifiers
rows.operation_detail: Explored analog hyperparameter combinations on image classification datasets.
rows.locator: Results and Discussion, Hyperparameter Exploration for Small-Scale Analog Neural Networks
rows.note: Reported as the maximum simulated accuracy for CIFAR10 across the tested combinations. Test accuracy does not show whether training classification error reached zero.
rows.check: 58.67% is a selected maximum test accuracy across heterogeneous hyperparameter settings, not an individual condition or training-error measurement. The subject pools linear and convolutional models.

rows.subject: 1- to 6-layer photonic analog image classifiers
rows.locator: Results and Discussion, Hyperparameter Exploration for Small-Scale Analog Neural Networks
rows.note: The paper states test accuracy increased to 77% for 50 epochs; this is not a training-error measurement.
rows.check: 77% is supported as test accuracy after 50 epochs, but the text does not establish a matched-model comparison with R1's selected 10-epoch maximum.

rows.subject: 9-layer convolutional neural network
rows.operation_detail: Converted and trained the model as an analog counterpart using AnalogVNN.
rows.baseline: Original full-precision digital model: 86.24±0.19% after training
rows.value: Unable to achieve a maximum test accuracy above 70%
rows.locator: Results and Discussion, Applying AnalogVNN to Large Analog Neural Network Models (9-layer)
rows.note: The initial analog model result motivated testing additional hyperparameters. Test accuracy does not show training error.
rows.check: The analog result is an upper bound on initial test accuracy. The 86.24±0.19% digital baseline is attributed to reference [8], not established as a matched control trained in this study.

rows.subject: 9-layer convolutional neural network
rows.operation_detail: Trained the analog model with optimized hyperparameters.
rows.locator: Results and Discussion, Applying AnalogVNN to Large Analog Neural Network Models; Figures 6 and 7
rows.note: The text describes optimized hyperparameters and figured test-accuracy results, but gives no numerical final accuracy in prose. This is not a training-error measurement.
rows.check: Figure only is not a result value. Figures 6–7 contain multiple conditions and measures that should not be pooled into one result row. The explicit finding that learning requires at least 4-bit weights could replace this placeholder, but bears on none of V1–V6.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
